Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
Key features: VIX very high, credit spreads wide, equities down sharply, dollar strong, policy rate rising (+1 over 12m), and 2-year yield high. The unemployment rate is low (-1.5), though it has risen over 3 months. Headline CPI is low relative to its 3-year average, and core CPI is average. Industrial production is weak.

Candidates: late 2018 (December 2018), when equities fell, VIX spiked, the Fed was hiking, the dollar was strong, and unemployment was at a low. Headline CPI was low versus its 36-month average (oil fell). Credit spreads widened. The 2-year yield was high relative to its 3-year average. The 10-year yield was near its average. The 10y-2y spread was flat-ish. Gold was +1 over 1 month (December 2018 gold up about 5%). US equities 1m -2.5, which fits December 2018 (-9%). Industrial production -1.5 doesn't fit well for 2018, though. Payrolls were strong, however.

An alternative is 2015 or August 2015, but the policy rate was then at zero. Dec 2018 seems best, though 12m equity returns would be around -4%, which fits a z of -2.5. Treasuries 7-10y 3m +0.5 fits too.

Industrial production -1.5 might be odd, but the 36-month window includes the strong 2018 data. Maybe this is a different month, such as the 2018-12 vs 2019-01 comparison. I'll go with December 2018.
